# Test fixtures

## `fsrs-reference.json`

Ground truth for the FSRS-6 port, generated by running the reference
implementation — [open-spaced-repetition/py-fsrs](https://github.com/open-spaced-repetition/py-fsrs)
(MIT) — and recording its output across every branch of the core math.

`fsrs.test.mjs` asserts our JavaScript matches it, and the same numbers are
exported into the Swift test vectors, so the Swift port is validated against the
real algorithm rather than against our reading of it.

To regenerate after an FSRS version bump:

```sh
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/open-spaced-repetition/py-fsrs /tmp/py-fsrs
pip install typing_extensions
cd /tmp/py-fsrs && python3 - <<'PY' > fsrs-reference.json
import sys, json; sys.path.insert(0, '.')
from fsrs.scheduler import Scheduler
from fsrs.rating import Rating
s = Scheduler()
out = {'decay': s._DECAY, 'factor': s._FACTOR, 'cases': []}
for rating in [1, 2, 3, 4]:
    out['cases'] += [
        {'fn': 'initial_stability', 'rating': rating,
         'v': s._initial_stability(rating=Rating(rating))},
        {'fn': 'initial_difficulty', 'rating': rating,
         'v': s._initial_difficulty(rating=Rating(rating), clamp=True)},
    ]
for st in [0.5, 2.0, 8.2956, 50.0]:
    for el in [0, 1, 7, 30, 365]:
        out['cases'].append({'fn': 'retrievability', 'stability': st, 'elapsed': el,
                             'v': (1 + s._FACTOR * el / st) ** s._DECAY})
    out['cases'].append({'fn': 'interval', 'stability': st,
                         'v': s._next_interval(stability=st)})
for d in [1.0, 5.0, 6.4133, 10.0]:
    for rating in [1, 2, 3, 4]:
        out['cases'] += [
            {'fn': 'next_difficulty', 'difficulty': d, 'rating': rating,
             'v': s._next_difficulty(difficulty=d, rating=Rating(rating))},
            {'fn': 'short_term_stability', 'stability': d, 'rating': rating,
             'v': s._short_term_stability(stability=d, rating=Rating(rating))},
        ]
for d in [2.0, 5.0, 9.0]:
    for st in [1.0, 10.0, 100.0]:
        for r in [0.3, 0.7, 0.95]:
            for rating in [1, 2, 3, 4]:
                out['cases'].append({
                    'fn': 'next_stability', 'difficulty': d, 'stability': st,
                    'retrievability': r, 'rating': rating,
                    'v': s._next_stability(difficulty=d, stability=st,
                                           retrievability=r, rating=Rating(rating))})
print(json.dumps(out))
PY
```

Then `npm test` and `npm run vectors`.

## `sample-words.csv`

A handful of hand-written entries for exercising the importer. Definitions are
original, so nothing here carries a licensing question — the real bank does, see
`docs/02-word-bank.md`.
